paper.title_en: Binary pulsar studies with multi-wavelength sky surveys. II. Companion star follow ups
paper.abstract_en: The identification of the stellar companions to binary pulsars and the extraction of the physical information encoded in their optical spectra are key to study the evolution of the binary system and how this is influenced by the interactions between the two stars. Obviously, extending the characterisation of the companion star spectra over an as large as possible wavelength range allows one to maximise the amount of information. In Paper I, we used 11 source catalogues built upon multi-wavelength (optical, infrared, ultraviolet) imaging sky surveys to search for the stellar companions of 144 field binary pulsars (i.e. not in Globular Clusters) selected from the Australia Telescope National Facility (ATNF) pulsar catalogue. For nine of these pulsars, for which the companion star had been already identified, we obtained new spectral information from imaging photometry in the surveys' bands. In particular, for some of these pulsars we provided the first possible detections of the companion star in either the ultraviolet or mid-infrared. Here, we serve this additional flux information as a base to update the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the companion stars and the multi-epoch catalogue photometry to look for flux modulation at the orbital period of the binary system.
